catalog_quote: A. Acento. Consideramos que el acento en esta lengua es un rasgo suprasegmental que caracteriza la palabra (ver definición de la palabra en el capítulo de Morfología). El acento permite distinguir palabras lexemáticas simples de palabras morfológicamente complejas. Fonéticamente el acento kogui es de intensidad aunque conlleva rasgo de altura, notoria sobre todo en palabras acentuadas en la última sílaba, cuando ésta es un morfema gramatical. La mayor parte de las palabras monomorfemáticas del kogui, tiene el acento en la penúltima sílaba y son bisílabas. Hay un pequeño porcentaje de palabras bisílabas agudas y de palabras esdrújulas. Existe oposición entre lexemas debida a la posición del acento, que se puede demostrar: ˈkala 'paja' / kaˈla 'pierna'; nugi 'cal del poporo' / nuˈgi 'peste' 'loco'; munʒi 'mujer' / munˈʒi 'malanga' (tubérculo comestible); mugi 'hinchado' / muˈgi 'ñeque' (Dasiprocta sp.) ... b. El acento sobre la última sílaba de la palabra verbal tiene una función gramatical: indica el pretérito. c. Cuando la palabra tiene gramemas sufijados que son acentuados, el lexema pierde su acento propio en beneficio de dicho gramema que atrae el acento de la palabra: /ˈinʒi miklunaˈki/ '¿no quieres yuca?' ... el morfema negativo-interrogativo ki lleva el acento de la palabra, y desaparece el del lexema nuni.

new_statements.translation: Phonetically the Kogui accent is one of intensity although it carries a pitch feature, noticeable above all in words accented on the last syllable when this is a grammatical morpheme. Most monomorphemic words of Kogui have the accent on the penultimate syllable and are disyllabic. There is a small percentage of oxytone disyllabic words and of proparoxytone words. There is an opposition between lexemes due to the position of the accent, which can be shown: kala 'straw' / ka'la 'leg'; nugi 'poporo lime' / nu'gi 'plague', 'crazy' [...] c. When the word has suffixed grammatical morphemes that are accented, the lexeme loses its own accent in favour of that morpheme, which attracts the word accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level stress (intensity) accent. Default/majority pattern: penultimate syllable in monomorphemic words (mostly disyllables), but position is lexically contrastive (minority of final- and antepenult-stressed words, minimal pairs). In complex words the accent moves: inherently accented suffixes attract the single word accent; verb-final accent marks the preterite. SIL orthography (Gawthorne & Hensarling 1984 §7) corroborates: the accent mark is written only when stress is NOT penultimate.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In compound words of four or more syllables a secondary accent is perceived on the syllable that bore the accent of the lexeme in its free form (p. 760).
new_statements.exceptions: A 'small percentage' of oxytone disyllables and proparoxytones; lexical minimal pairs (kála/kalá 'straw/leg', núgi/nugí, múnʒi/munʒí 'woman/malanga', múgi/mugí); accented suffixes (e.g. negative-interrogative -kí) override the lexeme's accent; final accent on verbs = preterite.
new_statements.domain_note: The word (defined on p. 766 as the stretch of speech carrying one accent); statement concerns monomorphemic citation forms, with separate rules for compounds and suffixed words. Author treats accent as distinctive; a stricter reading would be 'lexical with penultimate default'.
new_statements.identity_note: Ortíz Ricaurte 2000 describes Kogui as spoken on the northern slope of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (data mainly from mama Juan Conchacala Dingula, San Miguel/Anche-Palomino-Don Diego valleys); same language as Glottolog cogu1240 (Kogi/Cogui/Kággaba, ISO kog); no dialect split is made.

new_statements.quote: Hay palabras Agudas : allunká, palma ; guanyék, basta ! siguí, esposo ; tokó, peso ; kushú, cresta. Graves : abáma, abuelo ; at-háse, ciento ; káulli, grito ; háso, sobrina ; háku, madrastra. Esdrújulas : Dulláshiaka, Religión ; síndulli, tominejo ; kuíbullu, pueblo. Sobre esdrújulas : nínguituka, vereda ; núsaguetse, feo ; huillákallalli, cañaveral ; háguibullu, cascajal.
new_statements.translation: There are words [that are] Oxytone (final-stressed): allunká 'palm', guanyék 'enough!', siguí 'husband', tokó 'peso (coin)', kushú 'crest'. Paroxytone (penult-stressed): abáma 'grandfather', at-háse 'hundred', káulli 'shout', háso 'niece', háku 'stepmother'. Proparoxytone (antepenult-stressed): Dulláshiaka 'religion', síndulli 'hummingbird', kuíbullu 'village'. Pre-proparoxytone (stressed on the fourth syllable from the end): nínguituka 'path', núsaguetse 'ugly', huillákallalli 'reed-bed', háguibullu 'gravel-bed'.

new_statements.relation_note: Same type as the existing statement from Ortíz Ricaurte 2000 (lexical, contrastive accent position; most monomorphemic words penult, with oxytone and proparoxytone minorities, and accent shifts induced by accented suffixes / preterite final accent). Celedón's graves class matches her penult majority, his agudas and esdrújulas her minorities, and his p. 84 verb note her morphological accent shifts. He adds a 'sobreesdrújula' (pre-antepenult) class, which she does not name separately (her closest remark is secondary accent in compounds of 4+ syllables). He gives no frequencies and no rule, so he does not contradict the catalog's lexical reading; the catalog record's rule field is currently em…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Celedón gives no placement rule; he simply sorts Kággaba words into the four Spanish-grammar accent classes (agudas / graves / esdrújulas / sobreesdrújulas) with examples, i.e. accent may sit on the final, penult, antepenult or pre-antepenult syllable and is a property of each word. Accent is marked with an acute throughout the grammar and vocabulary (p. 1 lists 'ó ú acentuadas' among the vowel signs). Footnote 1 on p. 84 ('Cuando en un verbo infinitivo cambia el acento para el participio ó imperativo, se ponen éstos en el renglón que siga') shows that accent position shifts with verbal morphology, and the numerals section notes that in makainüiñ '4 days' the root núi 'sun, day' keeps its shape 'aunque variado el acento'.
new_statements.exceptions: No rule, so no exceptions as such; the accent classes themselves show final, penult, antepenult and pre-antepenult accent. Morphological accent shifts noted for verbs (infinitive vs. participle/imperative, p. 84 n. 1) and for a numeral compound (makainüiñ).
new_statements.identity_note: Celedón writes 'lengua köggaba' (Kággaba), the autonym for Kogi/Kogui [kog], based on his 1880s missionary work in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta; same language as the catalog item, no dialect named. His transcription is Spanish-based (ll, sh, ö, ü, iñ/uñ for nasal vowels).

sources.note: Not established: an unpublished SIL-circle re-analysis of Kogi phonology (with morphophonemics and orthography) known only from its bibliography entry in Jackson 1995: 69; no record, abstract or copy is reachable. As a full phonology of Kogi it would at most restate the word accent (Ortiz Ricaurte 2000: intensity accent 'que conlleva rasgo de altura'; Gawthorne & Hensarling 1984: accent the only suprasegmental phoneme); no lexical-tone claim is expected, but its suprasegmental content is unknown.
